summary: Country Island light off Country Harbour, Nova Scotia: first lit 1873, an octagonal concrete tower built 1963 to 1965, the Coast Guard station closed to visitors.

structures.note: Square tower, 28 ft, attached to a keeper's dwelling. Lantern room damaged in transit and replaced in 1872-73 (Lighthouse Friends). Fixed white light, 51 ft above the sea.
Square two-storey dwelling with a lantern room on a hipped roof (Lighthouse Friends).

Octagonal concrete light tower, work begun November 1963 and completed 1965, with three dwellings and a fog-alarm and radio-beacon building (Lighthouse Friends). Standard lighthouse plan developed by the Department of Transport in 1954 (heritage statement). White, red top (Coast Guard list).

staffing.note: Last keeper, Clyde M. Lahey, left 29 September 1986 (Lighthouse Friends).

access.note: The Coast Guard owns the light. Grounds and tower closed; best seen from the water (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Square lighthouse and keeper's dwelling built; contract to James McDonald, $1,295; lantern room $373.
Light put into operation 1 May 1873 (Lighthouse Friends).
Great Nova Scotia Cyclone, 24 August 1873: shed at the landing destroyed, road blocked, plaster shaken loose; tower braced with wire rope (Lighthouse Friends).
Larger lantern room and new lighting apparatus (Lighthouse Friends).
Stone foundation rebuilt with cement mortar; dwelling enlarged (Lighthouse Friends).

In fiscal 1907-08 the Department had a set of lighthouses repainted with white and red stripes or bands, to make them more conspicuous when snow is on the ground; the 1909 report (printed p. 67, scan 76) names Country harbour.
Changed from fixed white to a flashing light: a pair of flashes nine seconds apart, then 27 seconds of darkness (Lighthouse Friends).
Original lighthouse replaced after 55 years by a square two-storey dwelling with a lantern room (Lighthouse Friends).

Octagonal concrete light tower, dwellings and fog-alarm building; work begun November 1963, completed 1965; old lighthouse demolished (Lighthouse Friends). Heritage statement dates the 1960s rebuilding.
400-watt electric horn replaced the diesel engines and compressors that drove the diaphone; station reduced to two keepers.
Submarine cable brought commercial power; Lighthouse Friends says this made automation possible.
Diesel generators and fog detector moved inside; last keeper left 29 September 1986.
Country Island and surrounding waters declared a protected area to safeguard roseate terns (Lighthouse Friends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1873 (first light, Lighthouse Directory and Lighthouse Friends) and 1963 or 1965 (present tower). Lighthouse Friends gives the tower built 1872, the light lit 1 May 1873, and the octagonal concrete tower begun November 1963 and completed 1965. Both are kept: 1873 for the first light and 1963 to 1965 for the present tower.
The Coast Guard list gives Fl W 20s, as the record does. OpenStreetMap's LFl W 20s is not used.

notes_for_editor: Rich secondary account (Lighthouse Friends) with a heritage statement, the Coast Guard list and two Department of Marine reports from the corpus. The 1873 cyclone account, the 1910 flash change, the 1927 dwelling, Kendrick's 1865 remark and the early keepers come from Lighthouse Friends only; the Department's 1874 and 1911 reports are not in the corpus and were not checked. The 1865 Kendrick passage is quoted by Lighthouse Friends from the 1865 report, which was not read. The 1902 keepers' table row for Giffin is OCR: the name prints as 'Critfin' and the row is matched by position (station, date and salary on one printed row). Henry Burke's Department table entries (1904, 1906, 1911) were not matched to this station and are not footnoted; his dates rest on Lighthouse Friends. Post-1960 keepers and the assistant (Keith Guptill, Vernon Zwicker, Terry Edmunds, Clyde M. Lahey, Don Crooks, Jim Guptill) are listed in public role only; Lighthouse Friends' personal reminiscences of the Guptill family are left out. Roseate tern protected area (2017) is Lighthouse Friends only. Web searches: 1. Page reads: about 3, plus corpus greps. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 1902 keepers' table row was read on the page image (printed p. 149, scan 260): Giffin, Spencer H. / Country Harbour, Green Island / Sept. 18, 1883 / 400 00. The OCR prints the name as 'Critfin'. The 1909 repaint list (printed p. 67, scan 76) was also read on the image. The Department's 1874 and 1911 reports are not in the corpus, so the 1910 flash change and 1927 dwelling still rest on Lighthouse Friends alone.
